content:
Hello

I'm just starting with verso (and to be honest, with lean in general) and I wanted to have a small, and very simple blog, mainly to document my own understanding of the subject I'm studying.
Seems a very reasonable objective to me, and verso seemed perfected for the job.
The problem is I can't seem to get anything working ... I couldn't find a single example using mathlib inside a verso blog/book. I've tried also the docstring path (which is ok, but I preferred the verso markup) but I can't seem to get it working either (maybe with more time I can get it to work properly, but I don't feel like wasting more time just yet).

Now that you have all the context, I'd like to know
a) How am I supposed to use Mathlib in a normal markup file? (in general, how do imports work)
b) Are lean code blocks supposed to be used this way?
c) What's your suggested workflow? Stick to docstring? Use markup but in some clever way I don't know of?
d) Do you have any project to share with me I can use as a reference?

Thank you

Hi @Roberto Zucchelli , thanks for the feedback. I fully agree we need to improve the onboarding experience, we are on it.

Have you seen https://github.com/leanprover/verso-templates ? This doesn't solve all the questions you have answered, but that's a first step.

In general, for working with Mathlib from Verso you have two options:

  • have mathlib inside the Verso dependency path. This is a bit heavy sometimes, as building the blog will require a mathlib build, but often pays off as you can access all info about Mathlib definitions.
  • elaborate mathlib definitions outside the Verso document, produce a .json file with the metadata, which can be read by the Verso document. This is often called an "anchor" on Verso parlance.

Could you elaborate more on how exactly you'd like things to work?

Hi @Emilio Jesús Gallego Arias, thank you for taking the time to look into this.
Yes, I've seen the templates, but unfortunately things immediately break as I try to go slightly offtrack (probably because the documentation is not crystal clear about how things are supposed to work). By the way, it's perfectly understandable that the onboarding experience, is a bit rough, from my understanding this is all kind of new + the ecosystem is still small.

To elaborate further my objective: I would prefer not to rebuild mathlib, I'm fine with limited info for the mathlib stuff in the final doc, my main objective is to surround my lean code with a proper explanation (text-book like).
My current attempt was to write the blog text + math content (lean) directly all in one markup file, without additional .lean files for the math. But maybe this is just not how that is supposed to work, is not very clear to me what is the scope of the "lean blocks".

Could you elaborate what the setup for your second option would look like?
To be clear, I'm all for the "simplest solution to get the job done".
I like the idea of a blog-like final product, but my main concern is studying, if I have to spend more time dealing with the setup and management than the rest, not really worth it for me right now. If achieving a blog-like result is too time consuming, I may stick to doc-strings (but right now I get an error when I try to run lake query :literateHtml, which seems to be the only step suggested by https://verso.lean-lang.org/doc/latest/Literate-Programming/#literate, aside from adding verso to [[require]], of course)
